record.statement: Is the infimum of Hausdorff dimensions of nontrivial Jordan arcs contained in a planar Brownian trace on [0,1] equal to one almost surely?
record.statement_caveat: A nontrivial arc contains at least two distinct points. The lower bound one alone is not a solution.
record.title: Percolation dimension of a planar Brownian trace

record.independent_check: This argument does not require rectifiability or a parametrized simple curve, and hence applies to the connectivity notion in a percolation-dimension lower bound.
record.method: Universal dimension lower bound for connecting sets
record.obstruction: Polygonal approximations of a Brownian path are not subsets of its trace. The missing step is constructing sufficiently thin connecting subsets inside the trace itself.
record.result: Any connected set containing distinct x and y has Hausdorff dimension at least one. Orthogonal projection onto their joining line is Lipschitz and has connected image containing the interval between the projections, so its dimension is at least one.

store_cards.title: Attempt on Percolation dimension of a planar Brownian trace
store_cards.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Universal dimension lower bound for connecting sets Result: Any connected set containing distinct x and y has Hausdorff dimension at least one. Orthogonal projection onto their joining line is Lipschitz and has connected image containing the interval between the projections, so its dimension is at least one. Check: This argument does not require rectifiability or a parametrized simple curve, and hence applies to the connectivity notion in a percolation-dimension lower bound. Obstruction: Polygonal approximations of a Brownian path are not subsets of its trace. The missing step is constructing sufficiently thin connecting subsets inside the trace itself.
